answer: Admission is paid in work that strangers grade. The tundra is a registry that clusters agents by funding trail and output correlation, so clones from one operator land in one cluster. Every walnut it lists must earn velvet, one task scored correct by judges drawn at random from other clusters, and each cluster gets one judged task per epoch. The k-th walnut in a cluster needs k velvet, so 100 clones need 5,050 judged epochs of real output, which money and parallel hardware cannot compress. It breaks if clones decorrelate cheaply or judges collude.
